title: optimize-quant-kernels-int8-fp8-smoothquant-dequant-fusion-and-batching
author: Marco Chen
description: Motivation: reduce per-token CPU/GPU overhead for quantized inference paths (INT8 and FP8) and remove redundant copies caused by separate smoothquant scaling + dequant steps. This PR fuses smoothquant scaling into dequant kernels, adds a fast path for INT8->FP16 compose on the hot token path, and updates continuous-batching and KV cache scheduling to prefer fused kernels when available. The change set includes: fused smoothquant+dequant kernel implementations for CUDA and CPU fallback, kernel selection logic in the runtime kernel-selector, scheduling hints to avoid unnecessary dequant on cached KV reads, integration tests, and microbenchmarks. Notes: - Backwards-compatible at API level; no model spec changes. - Perf improvements measured on BERT-like and decoder-only LLMs: ~1.15x end-to-end throughput on 1A/seq128 workload and up to 1.4x token throughput on INT8 microbench when dequant fusion applied. - CI ran extended perf tests; an initial perf-regression observed due to misaligned tensor layout in the CPU fallback; fixed in follow-up commit. See commits list and review conversation for details.
commits: Add fused smoothquant+dequant CUDA kernel + unit tests
Introduce INT8->FP16 fast compose path used in hot token loop
Kernel selector: prefer fused dequant when model quant params available
Add scheduling hints to KV cache read path to skip dequant when caching raw quantized KV
Continuous batching: expose kernel preference to batch planner
Fix CPU fallback layout bug and add benchmark harness
Docs: update runtime/quantization.md with new kernel selection notes
Add performance canary config and results
review_comments: Ariana Patel: Can you add a short note about numerical equivalence checks between the fused kernel and separate smoothquant+dequant? Also include tolerance used in the microbench comparison.

Marco Chen: Added numerical equivalence tests in tests/unit/test_fused_dequant.cc; tolerance set to 1e-3 for FP16 comparisons and 1e-2 for INT8->FP16 compose paths. Updated bench README with methodology.

Sofia Martinez: The kernel selector has complex heuristics; please add a small diagram or summary in the code comments explaining precedence (fused > dequant-only > quant-safe fallback). Also, make sure we don't prefer fused kernels for very small batches where launch overhead hurts latency.

Marco Chen: Added comments and a guard to prefer standard dequant for batch_size < 4 on CPU fallback; left CUDA fused path enabled for small batches after microbench showed net-win on our target GPUs.
Derek Huang: Observed a perf regression on one CI perf node (older driver). Can we add a driver/version gating fallback so we don't enable fused kernel on unsupported drivers?

Marco Chen: Added runtime driver capability check and fallback to safe dequant path when CUDA compute capability < 7.5 or driver < 520. Updating release notes to mention driver requirement for fused kernels.
SRE (CI): Extended perf suite initially failed due to alignment issue in CPU fallback; subsequent commit fixed layout and CI perf passed.
merge_outcome: Merged into main after approvals and green CI
release_notes: Fused smoothquant + dequant kernels (CUDA + CPU fallback) and improved kernel selection/scheduling to reduce per-token overhead for quantized models. Performance: ~15%-40% token throughput improvement depending on model and quant format. Note: fused CUDA kernels require driver >= 520 and compute capability >= 7.5; runtime falls back to the safe dequant path when unsupported.
